annotations.text:
SIGNING IN

The mark floats above the card and drifts gently; two more sit far back in the warm ground, barely there, moving on a slower cycle. Nothing spins or bounces — it should feel like the page is breathing.

No sign-up link, because nobody signs themselves up. If you have no account, an administrator makes one and sends you a link.

What the person sees when they tap the link you sent them. Their name is already there, so they know it is really for them.

One rule, stated once: at least 12 characters, and a short sentence is suggested rather than a list of symbol requirements.

HOME — NOW WITH THE GRAPH, AND NO MONEY

Cost is gone everywhere, as you asked. The third figure is Waiting to print instead, which is the thing someone actually wants to know.

The graph is two soft curves: what people sent from the app, and what was done standing at the machine. Those two are genuinely different things in the data, and the shape of the gap between them is the most useful thing on the page.

Spacing is the same everywhere now — 20px between cards, 18px corners, 22-24px inside them, one soft shadow. Every page in the build will use that same rhythm.

Same page, reordered for a thumb: the big blue action first, then whatever is wrong, then the numbers, the graph, and the printers.

Only the printers that need something are listed.

ACCOUNTS — EXACTLY THE FLOW YOU DESCRIBED

Create an account, get a link, press Copy link, send it however you normally reach that person. No email server involved, no password typed by you, nothing to remember.

Waiting to set a password is the list of people who have a link out. Each row copies its link again, makes a fresh one if it went stale, or removes the account.

A forgotten password is the same three moves: the menu beside their name makes a reset link, you copy it, you send it. That link signs them out everywhere the moment it is made.

This needs a small piece of backend that does not exist yet: a table of single-use tokens, and endpoints to make one, redeem it, and revoke it. Half a day, no email server, no new dependency.

Everything else on these screens is already there — the two roles, per-person printer permissions, forced password change, and sessions ending the moment an account is turned off.
